label: Poisons, oils and coatings tier list

items.verdict: DC11 con save for Poisoned; worth remembering in early Act 1 fights, but reactive and easily passed
DC11 con save for 1d4 delayed damage; safely ignored unless you have no other coating
DC13 for 1d6 at the end of the enemy's next turn; too marginal for your only coating slot
DC15 for 1d8 delayed; rated up ONLY because you can get it extremely early for the hardest opening fights
reliable DC19 but 1d10 delayed damage is irrelevant by Act 2, where poison immunity is everywhere; sell it
no-save fire resistance strip, MANDATORY for fire builds; a BUG lets you convert enemies to fire vulnerable via wet
stacking +1 to attack and damage plus magical damage for ten turns, with no downside at all
DC13 save-or-sleep on weapon hits can end a fight outright; one attempt per enemy due to inoculation
+2 to attack for ten turns, which he rates slightly above the Diluted Oil of Sharpness
DC11 Reduced is too unreliable to build around and the effect is negligible; better off sold
no-save -3 to spell attacks and save DCs plus disadvantage on concentration; nice to have for wizard fights
DC13 save-or-paralysed, the game's best condition; roughly a one-in-four chance to win an encounter for free
rated alongside Crawler Mucus as the unique non-craftable version of exactly the same paralysis effect
DC15 save-or-blinded as a coating, but only DC10 when thrown; weaker than Crawler Mucus or Drow Poison
DC11 but targets Charisma with no inoculation, so Bane lands reliably; a modest workhorse coating
no-save 3d6 fire explosion on any fire hit, and the explosions chain across grouped enemies
needs about four hits to trigger Frozen; he'd move it to A or S for a multi-damage-instance build
DC17 disadvantage on attacks with no inoculation, but Fog Cloud and similar do it with no save
